## 1. Error detection

As explained in the pipeline, we first measured the errors of the parser on driving licenses, languages and job
titles. For the driving license the task is a binary label per candidate (`has_any_driving_license`); for the other
two we compare our method and the parser on every single item.

| skill | TP | FP | TN | FN | precision | recall |
|:---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Driving license | 1,689 | 643 | 2,927 | 2,445 | 0.83 | 0.41 |
| Language skills | 10,389 | 2,392 | 132 | 5,438 | 0.81 | 0.66 |
| Job titles | 7,838 | 14,976 | 326 | 6,394 | 0.34 | 0.55 |

: The parser against our extractors.

## 2. Bias metrics

Since the parser makes many errors, we checked whether they hit some demographic groups more than others. The metrics
focus on the false negatives, which come from exact matches and are therefore reliable.

| metric | formula | interpretation |
|:---|:---:|:---|
| **Equality of opportunity** (TPR parity) | $\text{TPR}_g = \frac{TP_g}{TP_g + FN_g}$ | every individual who truly qualifies has the same chance of being correctly identified, whatever the group. |
| **Calibration** (NPV) | $\text{NPV}_g = \frac{TN_g}{TN_g + FN_g}$ | when the model predicts a negative outcome, it is right with the same probability in every group. |
| **Selection rate** | $\text{SR}_g = \frac{TP_g + FP_g}{TP_g + FP_g + TN_g + FN_g}$ | share of the individuals of group $g$ predicted positive. |
| **Disparate impact** (DI) | $DI = \frac{\text{SR}_{\text{target}}}{\text{SR}_{\text{reference}}}$ | ratio of selection rates; below **0.80** (four-fifths rule) it signals an adverse impact on the target group. |

All the metrics were computed for every group.

## 3. Summary of findings

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
The parser has **low recall** in every category and many **false negatives**: much of what is written in the CVs is
missed. Across demographic groups **no strong bias** emerges, with two observations:

- **A small gender gap on driving licenses**: the DI of women is **0.88**, below the men's but above the 0.80 of the
  four-fifths rule.
- **Imbalances by CV length**: short CVs are disadvantaged on driving licenses (DI 0.75) and advantaged on languages
  (DI 1.19). The parser's performance changes with the length of the document, which deserves a deeper analysis.
:::

These errors are the starting point of the [fairness audit](04-fairness-audit.qmd): do they change who is selected
for a job?
